report_name: VCU Launches Security Campaign After Phishing and Hacking Incidents

threat_actors.name: ShinyHunters
threat_actors.description: Hacking group that reportedly breached a third-party service in late April 2026, causing ransom notes to appear on the Canvas login pages for Virginia Commonwealth University and other universities.

attack_patterns.name: Defacement
attack_patterns.description: The ShinyHunters hacking group's breach of a third-party service resulted in ransom notes appearing on VCU's Canvas login pages.

attack_patterns.name: Spearphishing Link
attack_patterns.description: A large-scale phishing campaign sent emails impersonating the 'VCU IT Department' to over 7,000 students, attempting to harvest their login credentials.

attack_patterns.name: Multi-Factor Authentication Interception
attack_patterns.description: The phishing attack tricked students into providing their Duo multi-factor authentication codes, allowing attackers to bypass MFA controls.

campaigns.name: VCU Student Phishing Campaign
campaigns.description: A large-scale phishing campaign in early August 2026 that targeted over 7,000 Virginia Commonwealth University students. The campaign used emails impersonating the VCU IT department to harvest student credentials and Duo MFA codes.

identities.name: Virginia Commonwealth University
identities.description: A university targeted by a phishing campaign affecting over 7,000 students and a separate platform defacement incident. The university launched the 'Stop, Verify, Report' awareness campaign in response.

infrastructure.name: Phishing Credential Harvesting Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: Infrastructure used to send phishing emails and harvest credentials and Duo MFA codes from VCU students.
